title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
event_hint: Kairos: a load-aware prefill-deflection scheduler that runs deflected prefill in place on decode nodes to cut P95 TTFT up to 81% and eliminate inter-node KV-cache transfer in disaggregated LLM serving.
problem: Disaggregated LLM serving runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, which creates a new asymmetry: under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate and queue while decode nodes sit underutilized (decode is memory-bound with spare compute). On a 2P2D A100 cluster the authors show prefill execution is only 2-23% of P95 TTFT; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait and inter-node GPU-to-GPU KV-cache transfer, both scheduling artifacts rather than compute limits. Prior disaggregated designs (Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, TetriInfer) assume a request stays on its prefill node until prefill completes and then ships its KV cache to a decode node, so they cannot exploit the spare compute on decode nodes.
mechanism: Kairos is a proactive, time-aware prefill-deflection scheduler. For each queued request it estimates TTFT on the prefill node from current queue depth/order, and for every decode node sweeps candidate chunk-size sequences using an analytical TBT-safety model that predicts per-step decode latency from in-flight decode batch size, KV-cache occupancy, and added prefill chunk size (no live inference trials; one-time deployment-time profiling; no model changes). It deflects the request's prefill phase to a decode node when both (i) TBT safety holds (in-flight decode step latency stays within the TBT SLO tau, with margin beta) and (ii) projected decode-node TTFT is at most alpha times the prefill-node TTFT, where alpha >= 1 is a single operator-tunable knob (alpha=1 deflects only when the decode path is strictly faster). Algorithm 1 (PDF Page 9) formalizes this: build a TBT-safe chunk schedule per decode node via LargestSafe, pick the fastest feasible node, then deflect only if TTFT_dec(n*) <= alpha * TTFT_pf and TTFT_dec(n*) <= TTFT_slo (Eq. 7), else Keep. Deflected prefill runs as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with in-flight decode batches, so the prefill phase executes in place on the decode node and the inter-node KV-cache transfer is eliminated. Implemented on vLLM 0.18.1 (~2000 lines of Python); per-request scheduling overhead is below 1 ms at the prefill dispatcher.

evidence.claim: Prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT across the five workloads; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait plus inter-node KV-cache transfer (e.g., Bursty: 840.8 ms prefill queue, 1,070.1 ms prefill exec, 2,175.6 ms KV transfer, 7,893.9 ms end-to-end P95).
evidence.baseline: Canonical 2P2D disaggregated serving (2 prefill + 2 decode nodes), no deflection
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.1 Claim 2 and Table 3, PDF Pages 4-5

evidence.claim: Kairos reduces P95 TTFT by up to 81% and raises SLO attainment by up to 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers; the Section 6 evaluation names the baselines as PD Disaggregation (DistServe-style [21]) and TaiChi [18], run on the Bursty trace over RPS 6-12 where Kairos holds P95 TTFT/TBT SLO up to 9 RPS while PD disaggregation and TaiChi fall out earlier. Routing cost <1 ms per request.
evidence.value: up to 81% P95 TTFT reduction; up to 79% higher SLO attainment; <1 ms routing; SLO held to 9 RPS
evidence.condition: Bursty trace; RPS 6-12; SLO P95 TTFT<=4s and P95 TBT<=70ms; DeepSeek-V2-Lite; 2P2D A100 cluster; vLLM 0.18.1 (exact RPS/alpha of the 81%/79% maxima not stated in supplement)
evidence.source_locator: Abstract and Section 1, PDF Pages 1-2; Section 6.1.2 Baselines and 6.2/Figure 4, PDF Page 9

evidence.claim: Utilization is complementary: prefill SM utilization is 75-84% while decode SM utilization never exceeds 27%; the gap is widest in HPLD (84% prefill vs 7.5% decode), confirming decode-side compute slack available for chunked prefill.
evidence.condition: Five workloads; A100 80GB; measured via NVIDIA Nsight Systems
evidence.source_locator: Section 3 Claim 1 and Table 2, PDF Pages 3-4

evidence.claim: Injecting chunked prefill into decode batches keeps decode step-latency increase within 30 ms for chunk sizes up to 512 tokens across all workloads and batch sizes; for chunk sizes >= 1024 the first-chunk increase reaches about 30 ms (low-prefill regimes) up to about 50 ms (bursty/high-prefill regimes), so using large first chunks requires knowledge of cached-token volume.
evidence.value: delta T_step <= 30 ms for chunk size <= 512; up to ~50 ms for >= 1024
evidence.baseline: Decode step latency with no chunked-prefill injection
evidence.condition: Mixed prefill-decode batches on decode nodes across the five workloads

evidence.claim: Deflected requests execute prefill in place on the decode node, eliminating the inter-node KV-cache transfer; the system needs only one-time deployment-time profiling, no model changes, and imposes less than 1 ms per-request scheduling overhead (~2000 lines of Python on vLLM 0.18.1).
evidence.value: inter-node KV transfer eliminated for deflected requests; <1 ms routing; ~2000 LoC
evidence.baseline: Canonical disaggregated serving ships KV cache from prefill node to decode node
evidence.condition: Kairos on vLLM 0.18.1; 2P2D A100; deflected requests only
evidence.source_locator: Sections 1-2 Contributions and Design, PDF Pages 1-2; Algorithm 1, PDF Page 9

evaluation_context: Section 6 evaluation runs on Azure Machine Learning Compute Clusters using Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 nodes, each with 8x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs via NVLINK 3.0, AMD EPYC 7V12 64-core CPU, 900 GiB host memory; inter-node communication over InfiniBand and Azure Accelerated Networking. Topology is 2 prefill + 2 decode nodes (2P2D), with prior 1P3D / 3P1D comparisons on the Bursty workload. Model: DeepSeek-v2-Lite (MoE, 16B total / 2.4B active). Section 6 evaluates on the Bursty trace (most realistic, non-stratified) over RPS 6-12. SLO targets (both simultaneous): P95 TTFT <= 4 s, P95 TBT <= 70 ms. Section 6 baselines: PD Disaggregation (traditional DistServe-style [21], all prefill on prefill nodes) and TaiChi [18] (unified aggregation/disaggregation with differentiated GPU instances and flowing-decode scheduling). Q1 result: Kairos holds SLO up to 9 RPS while PD disaggregation and TaiChi fall out earlier. Per-request routing <1 ms; heartbeat interval = 100 ms; the decode-side single-deflection-per-heartbeat bottleneck requires RPS >= |decode nodes| / heartbeat (~20), far above the SLO-supported RPS, and is extensible by scaling decode nodes. Traces derived from a large-scale production LLM serving deployment (Company X); five workloads as in Table 1.
limitations: The headline 'up to 81% TTFT / 79% SLO attainment' are best-case figures from the abstract/contributions; Section 6 confirms the baselines (PD Disaggregation/DistServe-style and TaiChi) and the Bursty/RPS 6-12 condition but does not state the exact alpha or RPS at which the 81%/79% maxima occur, and at lower request rates Kairos behaves similarly to standard PD disaggregation (little gain). Evaluated on a single small cluster (2P2D, four A100 nodes) and a single model architecture (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, MoE); the full throughput-vs-RPS curve (Figure 5) and any pool sizes beyond 2P2D are not in the supplement. Benefit depends on decode-side compute slack and workload regime, and using chunk size >= 1024 for the first chunk requires cached-token-volume awareness. New caveat from supplement: if a request has a prefix already cached on a prefill node, deflecting it to a decode node loses that cached prefix, and Kairos currently does NOT account for prefix-cache residency in its TTFT estimate. The evidence reports GPU SM/TC/HBM utilization but not aggregate KV-cache bytes transferred or network-bandwidth utilization as outcome metrics; KV-transfer reduction remains stated qualitatively (eliminated per deflected request), not quantified.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to the TPN/KV-transfer topic: Kairos is a per-request, KV-cache-occupancy-aware scheduler that eliminates inter-node KV-cache transfer for deflected requests by running prefill in place on decode nodes, and it reports end-to-end P95 TTFT (up to 81% lower) and SLO attainment, which the topic values. Important boundary for project inference: Kairos is a GPU-pool/scheduling-side mechanism, not a network-side optimization; it avoids KV transfer rather than making the network faster, so it illustrates what scheduling alone can achieve and does not answer the topic's question about the irreplaceable value of network-side mechanisms. The visible evidence does not report network utilization, KV-transfer bytes, or TPOT as improved outcome metrics.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF (2607.02043v1) fetched; evidence covers abstract, intro/design (Pages 1-2), empirical study with Tables 1-3 and Figure 1 (Pages 3-5), and a partial throughput result (Page 10).
System is named Kairos in the body; the abstract describes it as a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler.

Repair supplement (PDF Pages 9, 11, 12) added Algorithm 1 (deflection decision), Section 6 setup/baselines (PD Disaggregation = DistServe-style [21]; TaiChi [18]), the Bursty RPS 6-12 eval with Kairos holding SLO to 9 RPS, the decode-bottleneck threshold (RPS >= |decode nodes|/heartbeat ~20), and the prefix-cache-residency-loss caveat. It did not state the exact alpha/RPS of the 81%/79% maxima, did not show the Figure 5 throughput curve, and did not quantify KV-transfer bytes/network utilization.

evidence_gaps.question: Which specific disaggregated scheduler is the baseline for the up-to-81% TTFT and up-to-79% SLO-attainment results, and under which workload, RPS, and alpha are those maxima achieved (versus non-bursty or lower-load cases)?

Does the paper quantify the KV-cache transfer reduction (bytes or transfers eliminated) or network-bandwidth utilization as an outcome, rather than only stating per-deflected-request elimination and GPU SM/TC/HBM utilization?

What is the full throughput-vs-RPS curve (Figure 5 text is truncated at '7 RPS'), and at what load or cluster scale do Kairos gains over PD disaggregation vanish; are results shown beyond 2P2D / four A100s?
